references.text: In [ref:1 Mos 41:55|Genesis 41:55], Pharaoh says to the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph! Do whatever he tells you." Mary's words to the servants—"Do whatever he tells you"—have a striking parallel to Pharaoh's words about Joseph, pointing to Jesus as the one who gives the bread of life and meets the people's needs.

In [ref:5 Mos 18:15|Deuteronomy 18:15], Moses promises that the Lord will raise up a prophet like him, and the people shall "listen to him." Mary's command to do what Jesus says points to the fulfillment of the promise concerning the prophet whom the people are to obey.

In [ref:Luk 1:38|Luke 1:38], Mary says, "Behold, I am the Lord's servant. Let it be done to me according to your word." Mary's own obedience to God's word in the Annunciation is reflected in her encouragement to the servants to obey Jesus.

In [ref:Joh 2:7-8|John 2:7–8], we see the immediate follow-through: the servants do exactly what Jesus commands, filling the jars with water and carrying it to the master of the banquet. This shows the fruit of Mary's call to obedience.

In [ref:Joh 14:15|John 14:15], Jesus says, "If you love me, keep my commandments." Obedience to Jesus' words is a recurring theme in the Gospel of John, and Mary's instruction at the wedding in Cana is the first indication of such obedience.

In [ref:Joh 15:14|John 15:14], Jesus says, "You are my friends if you do what I command." Mary's words to the servants to do what Jesus says foreshadow Jesus' own call to obedience as a mark of discipleship.
